Hi all — quick clarifications from the security/audit side: 

• Audit period: The SOC 2 Type II report covers the period October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025. The auditor tested operating effectiveness across that 12-month period for the controls in scope.

• Point-in-time controls: Any controls in the report that are described as "as of 9/30/2025" are being referenced as the report end date; however, the auditor's testing steps show operating effectiveness testing over the period for those control families unless explicitly stated otherwise in the control description. If you point to specific control IDs we can pull the exact auditor language and test steps.

• Bridge letter: Redwood can request a bridge letter (sometimes called a "subsequent events" letter) from our independent auditor to cover the gap from 2025-10-01 through 2026-01-31. A couple of practical notes:
  - Auditor approval required: the auditor must agree to issue a bridge letter and will typically require a short attestation from Redwood about any material changes.
  - Timing: once requested, auditors usually take ~7-10 business days to draft and finalize the bridge letter, assuming no material control changes.
  - Scope: the bridge letter will attest to the absence of material changes to controls; it is not a re-test of operating effectiveness.
  - Signatories: the auditor generally wants a named executive (CISO or Head of Security) and an operations owner to confirm no material changes. Monica — can you advise on the legal sign-off chain?

I've uploaded a short internal form we use to initiate the auditor request; if ACME would like to be copied to the auditor request, indicate the contact and we'll include them.

[attachment: Draft_Bridge_Letter_Request_Form.docx (DOCX, 120 KB)]

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through any of this.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
